title: Mistake, unsolicited benefits, and emergency intervention
shortTitle: Mistake, unsolicited benefits, and emergency intervention
summary: The restitution introduction distinguishes several reasons a benefit may be retained unjustly.
notes: A mistaken overpayment or mistakenly supplied service differs from a benefit deliberately forced on an unwilling recipient. The unsolicited musicians example explains the concern with bypassing feasible bargaining. Emergency medical services pose a different problem of intervention and price. The action names quasi-contract, quantum meruit, and quantum valebant have histories and sometimes imprecise usage; the basis for recovery should be stated directly.
